title: Quitting an app that sent a flood of notifications should stop the flood
line: Quitting an app that sent a flood of notifications now stops its popups right away; the notifications stay in history.
explanation: Plasma queues every notification it receives and shows the popups a few at a time, without caring whether the sending app is still running. When the app's D-Bus service went away, the model only removed the actions from its notifications, so a flood of queued popups kept appearing one by one long after the app was quit. Now the same service watcher also marks that app's notifications as expired, newest first: they leave the popup queue at once (queued ones never flash up) and stay in the history.

commits.message:
libnotificationmanager: expire notifications of apps that quit

When an app quit after sending a flood of notifications, the popups it
had queued kept showing up one by one. Now its notifications are marked
expired when its D-Bus service goes away, so they only stay in history.

BUG: 486070

media.caption: A chat-like app sends 40 notifications with an Open action and is quit at 0:02: the popups keep coming, one batch after another.
Same test with the fix: when the app quits, its popups close and no queued ones appear.
